changes.after: Use continue to skip one loop pass, or break to end the loop.

before: for (n in 1..4) assigns each progression value to n for that pass.
When n==2, continue proceeds to the next value without running the remaining body.
break leaves the loop instead of skipping only the current pass.
Unlabelled break and continue apply to the nearest loop. These examples use one loop so the target is clear.

after: Each pass through this `for` loop gives `n` the next number from 1 through 4.
The word `continue` skips the rest of the current pass. The loop then moves on to its next value.
The word `break` ends the loop. No later value is visited by that loop.
When loops are nested inside each other, a plain break or continue affects the nearest loop around it. This example has only one loop.
The screen shows `1`, `3`, and `4` on separate lines. When n is 2, continue skips the printing instruction.
To trace a loop, follow one value at a time. At each pass, ask whether the code prints, skips the rest of the pass, or ends the loop.

before.question: Replace continue with break. What prints?
choices: 1 only because the loop ends at 2.
before.explanation: break exits at the second value before it is printed.

after.question: Replace continue with break. What appears?
choices: Only 1, because the loop ends when n reaches 2.
after.explanation: The first pass prints 1. The second pass reaches break before println, so the loop ends there.
